question: How does google/embeddinggemma-2 enable a single text query to retrieve Markdown docs, PNG architecture diagrams, and 16kHz WAV audio files simultaneously?
options: By projecting Text tokens, Vision ViT patches, and 16kHz Audio Conformer representations through a shared Gemma 3n backbone onto the exact same 768-D unit hypersphere S^767
By deleting audio and image files
By converting text into MP3 files before searching
explanation: Because all three modality towers map into a shared L2-normalized 768-D vector space, inner product <q_text, v_modality> directly measures cross-modal semantic similarity.

question: What audio sample rate and channel configuration does the Gemma 3n / EmbeddingGemma-2 audio encoder expect?
options: 16 kHz mono PCM waveform converted into log-mel spectrograms
explanation: Speech and audio encoders in the Gemma 3n family operate on 16,000 Hz mono PCM waveforms transformed into log-mel spectrograms.

question: Since audio, image, and text vectors all live on the same unit sphere S^767, can you use an AUDIO embedding as the query vector to retrieve matching TEXT documentation or PNG diagrams?
options: Yes — inner product <v_audio, v_text> is symmetric on S^767, so any modality can query any other modality (Audio -> Text, Image -> Text, Text -> Audio/Image)
No — inner product only works when the left vector is text
Only if the audio file is smaller than 10 bytes
No — cosine similarity is not symmetric
explanation: Because <a, b> = <b, a> for any two unit vectors in S^767, a shared multimodal embedding space supports arbitrary any-to-any cross-modal retrieval.
